Let \(k\) be the number of edges intersected by the plane. The plane section is a convex \(k\)-gon, and each of its sides lies in a distinct face, so \(k\le F\).

For the polyhedron, every face has at least 3 edges, so counting face-edge incidences:
\[
3F \le 2E = 198,
\]
hence
\[
F \le 66.
\]
Thus \(k\le 66\).

This bound is attainable: take a bipyramid over a convex \(33\)-gon. It has \(E=3\cdot 33=99\) edges and \(F=2\cdot 33=66\) triangular faces. A plane can be chosen to cut all 66 faces, hence it intersects 66 edges.

\[
\boxed{66}
\]
